newsitem.title: FRANCE: France worried by Kinshasa's political ban.
newsitem.headline: France worried by Kinshasa's political ban.

text.p: France voiced concern on Tuesday that a ban on political activities in Kinshasa would hamper national reconciliation after months of war.
"The latest news from the Democratic Republic of Congo is worrying," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a news briefing.
"The suspension of all political party activity until further notice hardly seems to go towards national reconciliation and freedom of expression," he said.
President Laurent Kabila's administration has banned all political activities and public demonstrations in Kinshasa until further notice, citing a need to protect public security.

Rummelhardt said that U.S. State Secretary Madeleine Albright and French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette agreed when they met in Paris on Monday to work to help restore democracy and respect of human rights in the African country.

U.S. officials said on Monday that Albright is to send U.N. Ambassador Bill Richardson to Kinshasa to push Kabila to establish a broad-based government that would pursue economic and political reforms.

Rummelhardt said he believed French nationals in the former Zaire were not free to leave, and a senior French envoy had met them to discuss their concerns following the killing of two French businessmen in the wake of the takeover of Kinshasa by Kabila's troops.

Jean-Pierre Lafon, the foreign ministry official in charge of French residents abroad, met the secretary general of Kabila's AFDL and the new administration's foreign minister. He would meet the interior minister before returning to Paris to report to President Jacques Chirac.
